entities.name: PMID:27492636
observations: Longitudinal path-model study of 711 low-income, racially/ethnically diverse couples recruited after birth; depression measured at 1, 6, and 12 months postpartum and sleep quality at 6 months.

After adjustment for infant birth weight, breastfeeding, race/ethnicity, poverty, education, and immigration status, 1-month depressive symptoms predicted poorer 6-month sleep, while 6-month sleep quality predicted depressive symptoms at 6 and 12 months in partnered mothers, fathers, and single mothers.

Maternal sleep quality predicted paternal depressive symptoms at 6 and 12 months; abstract did not report standardized coefficients, confidence intervals, instruments, or whether paternal baseline depression was controlled for in that path.

entities.name: PMID:25524435
observations: Longitudinal study of 200 Hong Kong couples followed from pregnancy to 6 months postpartum; prenatal and partner depressive symptoms were associated with higher depressive symptoms in both parents at 6 months, but sleep was not the primary predictor in the retrieved evidence.

entities.name: PMID:36973695
observations: Longitudinal evidence indicates partner depressive symptoms can predict early postpartum symptoms; this supports symptom interdependence but does not directly establish sleep as the predictor or mediator.

entities.name: PMID:34169272
observations: Father-focused study used subjective and objective sleep measures and linked lower perceived sleep quality with paternal postpartum depressive symptoms, but the retrieved record did not establish longitudinal temporal prediction or distinguish concurrent association.

entities.name: Sleep predicts postpartum persistence
observations: In PMID:27492636, 6-month sleep quality predicted depressive symptoms at 12 months in partnered mothers, fathers, and single mothers, supporting prospective continuation of symptoms.
The same model showed 1-month depressive symptoms predicted poorer 6-month sleep, indicating a bidirectional sleep-depression cycle rather than sleep-only causation.

entities.name: Maternal sleep-father crossover
observations: In PMID:27492636, maternal sleep quality predicted paternal depressive symptoms at 6 and 12 months postpartum.
The result supports prospective within-couple crossover, but the retrieved abstract lacks effect sizes and does not clarify baseline paternal-depression adjustment for that path.
